To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
there exists a class of functions which is learnable by a finite learner, but not by a consistent learner.
there are functions which can be learned by a finite learner, which optimistically reflects its capability, but cannot be learned by a consistent learner, which reflects on its capabilities.

the class of recursive functions is learnable by a finite learner reflecting on its capability, and the class of primitive recursive functions is not learnable by an optimistic consistent learner reflecting on its capabilities.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following question: Can a learner, which reflects on its own capability, be more powerful than a consistent learner, which does not reflect on its own capability?

the following questions: What is the relationship between the classes of recursive functions learnable by a learner which optimistically or pessimistically reflects on its capabilities and the class of functions learnable by an arbitrary finite learner?
the following questions: (i) Can a consistent learner reflectively learn a function which cannot be learned by a consistent learner?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the following three classes of functions are incomparable: the classes of functions which are learnable by a finite learner, the classes of functions learnable by a learner that reflects on its capability and the classes of functions that can be learnt by an optimistic learner that reflects on the capability of the class.
the class of recursive functions is learnable by a finite reflective learner, but not learnably by a consistent reflective learner.

the reflective capability is more powerful than the consistency assumption, and that the consistency assumption does not help to solve the problem of the existence of a finite consistent learner for all classes of recursive functions which are learnable by some finite learner.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that there are classes of recursive functions which can be learned by reflective inductive inference, but not learnably by consistent inductive inference.
we show that reflective learning is not equivalent to optimistic reflective learning.
there exist classes which can be learned by a reflective learner, but not by a consistent learner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the notion of reflective learning is a useful tool in the study of learning problems which are not learnable by consistent learners.
the reflective inductive inference model is not closed under taking the intersection of two classes of functions, even if the classes are learnable by a reflective learner.
reflective inductive inference can be more powerful than inductive inference.
